audit_findings.title: Refinancing and securitization cash-sweep risk is absent from steady-state owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.319 billion of 2017 and 2018 notes has anticipated repayment dates in July 2027; failure to refinance adds at least $65.95 million of annual pre-tax interest (5% × $1.319 billion), plus the cash sweep
audit_findings.mechanism: Higher refinancing interest would reduce recurring equity-level owner earnings; a failed refinancing would redirect securitized cash flow away from common equity
audit_findings.evidence: If the Company has not repaid or refinanced the respective note series prior to the applicable anticipated repayment dates, additional interest of at least 5 % per annum will accrue, and the Company’s cash flows other than a weekly management fee to cover certain operating expenses would be directed to the repayment of the securitized debt.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual penalty and cash-sweep mechanism are demonstrated, but their occurrence is an unresolved possibility: Domino's expects to refinance and was satisfying its non-amortization tests at June 14, 2026. Nevertheless, the near-term principal concentration, minimum $65.95 million annual penalty, and potential loss of distributable cash are reasonably capable of materially reducing the valuation, so leaving the risk entirely outside the scenarios is material.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the valuation with the $1.319 billion July 2027 refinancing at documented market-rate spreads, then add a separate failed-refinancing case incorporating the minimum 5% additional interest and contractual cash sweep until repayment.

audit_findings.title: Contracted but uncommenced leases are not in the anchor cost base
audit_findings.magnitude: $161.6 million of undiscounted future minimum rentals was uncommenced at December 28, 2025; $96.5 million remained uncommenced at June 14, 2026; annual owner-earnings effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Future rent, finance-lease interest and maintenance costs reduce owner earnings, while the associated supply-chain capacity and productivity may increase earnings or growth
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 28, 2025 , in addition to the lease for the new supply chain construction on a standalone basis discussed above, the Company also had additional leases for certain supply chain real estate and certain supply chain vehicles that had not yet commenced.
audit_findings.explanation: The omitted future commitments are demonstrated, but total undiscounted commitments do not establish their annual expense, timing, or net economics. The decline from $161.6 million to $96.5 million, alongside $65.9 million of new finance-lease assets obtained during the first half of 2026, shows that part of the commitment had begun entering the accounts after the anchor year. Without the resulting capacity benefits and annual cost schedule, the record cannot determine whether the net valuation effect is material or even entirely negative.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the commencement dates, annual fixed and variable cash-rent schedule, finance-versus-operating classification, and expected incremental supply-chain earnings for each lease; rerun owner earnings using the net after-tax annual cost and benefit profile.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 is a mixed-perimeter anchor after a midyear refranchising
audit_findings.magnitude: 37 stores were refranchised in 2025 for $8.6 million of proceeds and a $4.0 million pre-tax gain; Company-owned revenue decreased $18.7 million and total FY2025 Company-owned store gross margin was $53.5 million; pro forma owner-earnings effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The perimeter change removes Company-owned store margin and maintenance capital while adding franchise royalties and changing working-capital requirements; any disposal gain affects the owner-earnings anchor if not purged
audit_findings.evidence: Revenues from U.S. Company-owned store operations decreased $18.7 million, or 4.8%, in 2025 primarily driven by the refranchising of the Maryland market in May 2025, but this decrease was partially offset by higher same store sales.
audit_findings.explanation: The mixed FY2025 perimeter is demonstrated, not hypothetical. Its materiality remains unresolved because the filing does not provide the transferred stores' operating profit, royalty replacement, maintenance capital or working capital. The entire Company-owned store gross margin was $53.5 million, or 9.6% of the $558.0 million owner-earnings anchor, and the 37 transferred stores were only a subset of that business; this bounds the direct store-margin exposure but does not measure the net pro forma effect. The additional 77-store refranchising in 2026 also makes a null perimeter assumption less representative at the valuation date.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a store-level pro forma FY2025 as if the 37-store transaction occurred at the start of the year, replacing store economics with royalties and removing associated maintenance capital and the $4.0 million gain; separately update the forecast perimeter for the 77 stores refranchised in 2026 and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The stated share ceiling does not capture maximum PSU payouts
audit_findings.magnitude: 46,571 target performance-based units disclosed at June 14, 2026 imply at most 46,571 additional shares above one-for-one inclusion at a 200% payout, equal to 0.138% of the 33.733594 million denominator; approximately $0.33 per base-case share
audit_findings.mechanism: Maximum PSU settlement increases the fully diluted share denominator and lowers value per share without changing aggregate equity value
audit_findings.evidence: These performance-based restricted stock units may vest three years from the date of grant, generally subject to the holder’s continued employment, and have time- and performance-based vesting conditions which provide for potential payouts of the target award amount between zero percent and two hundred percent, based on the Company’s three-year achievement as compared to the specified target performance conditions.
audit_findings.explanation: The ceiling is not literally a maximum because PSUs can pay at 200%, so the denominator error is demonstrated. On the latest filed target PSU count, however, the incremental maximum-payout shares are only 0.138% of the valuation denominator. Adding them would reduce the $238.64 base value by approximately $0.33 per share and cannot materially change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Separate current RSUs and PSUs, add 46,571 incremental shares for the maximum PSU payout, incorporate any post-quarter grants or cancellations, and recompute per-share values; no operating-value rerun is required.
